speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me; please describe the increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, and tell me exactly what you mean by episodes of pain when urinating. Additionally, please share more details about the history of your painful, swollen left ankle.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; your history of sexually active with inconsistent condom use, combined with recent monoarticular swelling followed by a new knee issue and urinary symptoms, is highly suggestive of an infection. I need to confirm if you have noticed any fever, chills, or redness over the joint, and whether the "pain with urination" feels like burning or pressure. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, Blood Cultures, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The clinical picture of a young sexually active male with sequential asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle then knee), dysuria, and significantly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, synovial WBCs) is classic for this post-infectious inflammatory condition. The presence of synovial neutrophilia rules out crystal arthropathy, and the specific history points away from septic arthritis or rheumatoid arthritis.
